Every source is recorded in notes/patch-sources.md. Add a product or an ingredient, push, and every player gets it the next time they're online.

steps: Pick a spot about the size of a quarter where it won't get rubbed or washed off, like the inside of your arm or the bend of your elbow.
Put on your normal amount, twice a day, for 7 to 10 days. For something you wash off, like a cleanser, leave it on for 5 minutes or as long as the directions say.
No redness, itching or swelling after 7 to 10 days? Go ahead and use it.
If your skin reacts, gently wash it off as soon as you can and don't use it again.
patchTest.note: Even products labelled "hypoallergenic", "natural" or "clean" can cause a reaction. Test one new product at a time.

source.name: American Academy of Dermatology: How to test skin care products

ingredients.name: Retinol
ingredients.what: A form of vitamin A. Skin converts it, step by step, into retinoic acid, the form cells respond to, so it's gentler and weaker than prescription retinoids.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Retinoid medicines have strong evidence for acne and sun-aged skin. Cosmetic retinol has much less: see the "Retinol for breakouts" claim.
ingredients.use: At night, a pea-sized amount for the whole face. Start a couple of nights a week and build up as your skin gets used to it. Sunscreen in the morning.
cautions: Dryness, redness and peeling are common in the first weeks
Don't start it at the same time as other strong products, like acids

sources.name: Review of 54 retinoid acne trials, 2019 (none of them retinol)
GoodRx Health: When to use retinol

ingredients.name: Adapalene
ingredients.what: A retinoid medicine sold without a prescription (0.1% gel) for acne. It changes how the cells lining the follicle grow and shed, so pores are less likely to clog.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Dermatologists strongly recommend topical retinoids for acne. Adapalene 0.1% was the first retinoid the FDA approved over the counter, for ages 12 and up.
ingredients.use: Once a day, a thin layer over the whole area where you get acne, not just on spots. Give it up to 3 months. Using more, or more often, doesn't work faster.
cautions: Dryness, redness and stinging are common in the first weeks
Don't use it on cuts, scrapes, eczema or sunburn
Limit sun and use sunscreen while you're using it
Under 12: ask a doctor

ingredients.name: Benzoyl peroxide
ingredients.what: An acne medicine that cuts down the acne bacteria on the skin. It comes in washes, creams and gels, usually from 2.5% to 10%.
ingredients.evidenceNote: One of the treatments America's dermatologists strongly recommend for acne.
ingredients.use: Start with a low strength and only go up slowly if you need to. Apply a thin layer just after washing, or use it as a wash.
cautions: Can dry and irritate skin
Can bleach towels, pillowcases and clothes
Store it as the label says: heat can break it down

sources.name: AAD acne guidelines, 2024 (summary)
Mayo Clinic: Nonprescription acne treatment
AAD: Acne diagnosis and treatment

ingredients.name: Salicylic acid
ingredients.what: A beta hydroxy acid that dissolves in oil, so it can get into oily pores. It loosens the dead cells that plug them.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Dermatologists' 2024 guideline gives it a conditional recommendation: it helps, but the evidence is weaker than for benzoyl peroxide or retinoids. Works best on blackheads and whiteheads.
ingredients.use: Sold from 0.5% to 2%, as washes and leave-on products. Follow the label.
cautions: Mild stinging and irritation are possible
Go easy if you also use other acids or retinoids

sources.name: Mayo Clinic: Nonprescription acne treatment
AAD: Adult acne treatment dermatologists recommend
Dermatology Times: AAD's 2024 acne guidelines

ingredients.name: Glycolic acid
ingredients.what: An alpha hydroxy acid (AHA). It loosens the dead cells on the surface so they shed faster, which can make skin feel smoother.
ingredients.evidenceNote: It does exfoliate. The FDA found that AHAs make skin more sensitive to the sun while you use them and for up to a week after.
ingredients.use: Follow the label. Use sunscreen, cover up and limit sun while using it and for a week after you stop.
cautions: Raises sunburn risk
Can burn, sting or irritate, especially at high strengths
Don't pile it on with other acids or retinoids

sources.name: FDA: Alpha hydroxy acids
FDA guidance: labelling cosmetics that contain AHAs

ingredients.name: Niacinamide
ingredients.what: A form of vitamin B3. Studies suggest it helps the barrier hold on to water and can reduce oiliness.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Some trials support barrier and oil benefits. For acne, a review found the evidence unclear because there are few good studies. Usually well tolerated.
ingredients.use: Follow the label. It's in many moisturizers and serums, often at 2% to 10%.
cautions: Usually well tolerated; stop if it irritates

sources.name: DermNet: Nicotinamide
Review: Nicotinic acid/niacinamide and the skin, 2004
Review: The role of nicotinamide in acne treatment, 2017

ingredients.name: Vitamin C
ingredients.what: An antioxidant. The most studied form, L-ascorbic acid, breaks down in air, heat and light, and only gets into skin well in a very acidic product.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Some studies show benefits for sun-aged skin and dark spots, but the versions in products differ a lot and many are less studied.
ingredients.use: Follow the label. Keep it closed, cool and out of the light.
cautions: If it turns yellow or brown, it has broken down
Can sting

sources.name: Review: Topical vitamin C and the skin, 2017
Linus Pauling Institute: Vitamin C and skin health

ingredients.name: Hyaluronic acid
ingredients.what: A humectant: it holds on to water. Big versions stay on top of the skin and hydrate the surface; only smaller pieces get into the stratum corneum.
ingredients.evidenceNote: It does hydrate the surface. It doesn't refill the hyaluronic acid deep in the dermis.
ingredients.use: Follow the label. A moisturizer on top helps keep the water in.
cautions: Very well tolerated

sources.name: Harvard Health: The hype on hyaluronic acid
Study: skin penetration of hyaluronic acid by size, 2016

ingredients.name: Ceramides
ingredients.what: Fats that make up a big part of the barrier's mortar, with cholesterol and fatty acids. Moisturizers add them to help the barrier.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Moisturizers work by hydrating skin and helping restore its barrier. Ceramides are one of the barrier's own ingredients.
ingredients.use: Use the moisturizer as the label says, ideally on slightly damp skin.
cautions: Very well tolerated

sources.name: StatPearls: Moisturizers
StatPearls: The skin barrier and moisturizers

ingredients.name: Petrolatum
ingredients.what: An occlusive: a layer that slows water leaving the skin. It's the most effective one, cutting water loss through the epidermis by nearly 99%.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Well studied. It also slips into the gaps of the stratum corneum, and the barrier can recover normally underneath it.
ingredients.use: A thin layer, best on slightly damp skin, to lock the water in.
cautions: Feels greasy

sources.name: StatPearls: Moisturizers
Ghadially et al.: how petrolatum works in the stratum corneum, 1992

ingredients.name: Sunscreen filters
ingredients.what: The ingredients that absorb or scatter UV light. Zinc oxide and titanium dioxide are the mineral ones; the rest are called chemical filters.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Sunscreen prevents sunburn and sun damage. The FDA lists zinc oxide, titanium dioxide and bemotrizinol as safe and effective, and has asked for more data on the others; it hasn't found them harmful.
ingredients.use: Broad spectrum, SPF 30 or higher. Reapply every 2 hours outdoors, and after swimming or sweating.
cautions: Mineral sunscreens are recommended for sensitive skin
No sunscreen blocks 100% of UV

sources.name: AAD: Sunscreen FAQs
American Cancer Society: How to use sunscreen

ingredients.name: Fragrance
ingredients.what: Makes a product smell nice. It does nothing for your skin.
ingredients.evidenceNote: Fragrances are the most common cause of allergic reactions to cosmetics. Up to about 4.5% of adults are allergic to fragrance ingredients.
ingredients.use: If your skin is sensitive, pick fragrance-free products, and patch-test anything new.
cautions: Can cause allergic rashes, sometimes after years of use without problems
"Unscented" can still contain fragrance that masks other smells

sources.name: DermNet: Cosmetic allergy
Review: Fragrances, contact allergy and other effects, 2020
